contents.name: Initial histories, method of steps, and existence for retarded equations
contents.support: Confirms the constant-delay method-of-steps reduction and continuous-history convention. The local theorem proves the stronger stated globally state-Lipschitz existence and uniqueness bound directly.

contents.name: Aligned constant-step Runge–Kutta methods for retarded equations
contents.locator: Lecture 10, Theorem 10.1 and complete proof, PDF pp. 116–118
contents.support: The notes prove order preservation for a natural Runge–Kutta method when h divides the fixed delay and the data satisfy stronger smoothness assumptions. The assigned Euler theorem derives its own tube-dependent first-order bound under explicit time-Lipschitz and interpolation hypotheses.

contents.name: Bellman's method of steps and delay breakpoints
contents.support: Supports the locations of constant-delay breakpoints and the interval-by-interval ODE interpretation. The example computes its crossing-step RK4 defect explicitly and claims no general fourth-order DDE result.

contents.name: Neutral equations and the effect of derivative-delay feedback
contents.support: Provides the neutral-equation setting and the distinction between retarded and neutral smoothing. The assigned scalar compatibility, finite shift inverse, and Euler error proof are developed locally with their exact hypotheses.

contents.name: A finite-window distributed-delay integral and composite midpoint error
contents.locator: No matching section in this discrete-delay/neutral lecture treatment.
contents.reason: This source treats discrete delays and neutral equations; it does not provide the assigned finite-window integral convention or its midpoint quadrature estimate. Those items are supported by the full distributed-delay treatments below and complete local proofs.

contents.name: Neutral delay equations and derivative discontinuities
contents.support: Supports the neutral derivative-delay equation class and its distinction from retarded equations. The local scalar statement adds compatibility and the exact finite segment-shift convention.

contents.name: Distributed-delay equations as integral history inputs
contents.support: Supports the use of an integral over past values as a distributed-delay input. The local definition specifies a finite fixed window [0, tau] and a continuous kernel.

contents.name: Dense output, interpolation, and numerical treatment of delay breakpoints
contents.support: Supports the need to represent between-node delayed queries by a continuous extension. The local interpolation lemma proves its explicit vector-norm error constant.

contents.name: Numerical treatment of distributed delays and kernel quadrature
contents.support: Provides an independent numerical treatment of distributed-delay integral terms. Its Volterra/convolution setup differs from the fixed finite-window history functional here; the assigned midpoint rule and separate error split are proved locally.

contents.name: Bounded distributed delays and continuous history data
contents.support: Defines a bounded distributed delay over a compact interval of delay lengths, with the past state integrated against a weight. This is the same finite-window structural interface; the assigned vector-valued continuous-kernel variant is explicit locally.

contents.name: Replacing a distributed-delay integral by quadrature nodes and weights
contents.support: Confirms the integral-to-weighted-delayed-sample discretization. The paper discusses Simpson/Gaussian choices; this pair specifies composite midpoint and proves its separate history and quadrature errors directly.

contents.name: Exact error constant for the assigned midpoint and stored-history rule
